summary: The note describes how schools in a local district are prioritizing parental involvement in the academic year that began September 1, 2023. It covers communication channels, closing the digital divide, events, workshops, transparency, technology, face-to-face outreach, feedback loops, and culturally responsive practices. It concludes that continuous evaluation is needed and that families are now seen as essential partners in education.
one_line: Schools in a local district use varied communication strategies, workshops, events and outreach to boost parental involvement and student success in the 2023 school year.
key_facts: Parental involvement is linked to improved academic performance, better behavior, and enhanced social skills.
Principal Linda Simpson of Jefferson Elementary initiated the 'Partners in Progress' program on September 15.
Michael Johnson, IT director for the local school district, has implemented low-cost internet plans for low-income families since October 2023.
Computers have been placed in community centers and libraries so all parents can stay informed about their child's education.
Madison High School has successfully trialed family reading nights and math game evenings since the start of the term.
Isabella Torres, a family engagement consultant, works with the school district on parent workshops covering topics from digital literacy to understanding the school's curriculum.
Principal Simpson says transparency practices strengthened after September 1, including newsletters, Parent-Teacher Association meetings, and open-door policies, are crucial.
Andrew Li, a teacher at Lincoln Middle School, saw a surge in engagement after starting a weekly classroom blog.
Sarah Bennett, a middle school counselor, found that personal calls about a student's progress lead to profound conversations with parents that digital means alone would not produce.
As of November 2023, parent liaison officer James Franklin has seen a tremendous response to feedback forms, suggestion boxes, and parent councils.
Rosa Martinez, director of community outreach, has translated school materials and organized multicultural events since the start of the year.
Schools must continually evaluate and adapt their communication methods so they remain relevant and effective.
